1.explanation: The files prism-typescript.js and prism-tsx.js define Prism’s TypeScript and TSX grammars, including the regexes that match reserved keywords. The current keyword patterns don’t enforce a proper word boundary at the end of the match, so they incorrectly match the prefix of longer identifiers (e.g. matching “infer” inside “inference”). By correcting those regexes—adding or tightening the trailing boundary check—you will prevent partial matches and fix the highlighting issues. The .min.js files are the corresponding builds that also need updating once the source .js files are patched.
1.bug_scenario: In TypeScript/TSX import lists, identifiers that begin with a reserved keyword (e.g. “inference” or “typeDefs”) are being partially highlighted as if they were the bare keyword (“infer” or “type”), even though they’re part of a longer identifier. Only exact, standalone keywords should be highlighted.

2.explanation: Both prism-typescript.js and prism-tsx.js define the TS/TSX language grammars and supply the regexes that Prism uses to identify keywords. The bug stems from their keyword patterns not enforcing end-of-word boundaries, so they match reserved words when followed by alphanumeric characters. Adjusting the regex in these files (e.g. adding a word boundary \b at the end of the keyword patterns) will prevent partial matches like “inference” or “typeDefs.”
2.bug_scenario: In TSX/TypeScript imports, Prism’s TypeScript grammar is matching reserved words like `infer` and `type` inside longer identifiers rather than as standalone words. So when you write `import { infer, inference, infer }`, Prism flags both occurrences of “infer”—even the one in “inference”—as a keyword. The same happens with “type” (but not with “const” since its regex uses proper word boundaries).
